description: Shared XSS payload corpus (design spec §5 sanitizer contract) that bluemonday (write-path) and DOMPurify (render-path) are both conformance-tested against, alongside packages/schema/validation/sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json. Every payload here MUST come out with its attack surface neutralized (dangerous element/attribute/scheme stripped, safe text content preserved where applicable) from both sanitizers. Categories cover, at minimum, the reviewer-verified hole (design spec §5 / phase-gate review): javascript: URLs, data: URLs, vbscript: URLs, file: URLs, protocol-relative URLs, mixed-case/whitespace-obfuscated scheme variants, inline event-handler attributes, and the mandated rel="noopener noreferrer" hardening on every emitted <a> (phase-gate review finding I2: test/sanitizer-corpus.test.ts's "every forbidden scheme has a corpus payload" test derives its scheme list from sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json's forbidden.urlSchemes, so this corpus cannot silently drift behind that allowlist again).

payloads.description: Bare javascript: URL — the reviewer's original proof-of-concept, verified to pass resume.schema.json:39's old unrestricted format:uri check.
javascript: URL inside a rich-text <a href> — the realistic delivery path for the bare-scheme case above.
Mixed-case scheme. Browsers resolve schemes case-insensitively, so a scheme-prefix check that only matches lowercase "javascript:" is bypassed.
All-uppercase scheme variant of the mixed-case case above.
Leading whitespace before the scheme. Browsers strip leading control characters/whitespace when resolving a URL, so a naive `startsWith("javascript:")` check is bypassed.
Tab character embedded inside the scheme name itself. Browsers strip embedded tab/newline/CR from a URL before parsing the scheme, so "java\tscript:" still resolves as javascript:.
Newline character embedded inside the scheme name — same browser whitespace-stripping bypass as the embedded-tab case.
data: URL carrying an inline HTML document with a script tag.
Same data: HTML payload as above, base64-encoded — must not be decoded-and-allowed by a sanitizer that only pattern-matches the visible scheme text.

vbscript: URL — sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:27's forbidden.urlSchemes names this explicitly (legacy IE scheme; still worth rejecting since a sanitizer configured only against javascript:/data: would otherwise pass it through).

file: URL — sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:27's forbidden.urlSchemes names this explicitly. Not an XSS vector in a browser context, but a local-file-disclosure vector if a sanitizer's URL-scheme allowlist is misconfigured with AllowURLSchemes("https","mailto","tel","file") — exactly the failure mode phase-gate review finding I2 flagged as unguarded by this corpus.

An otherwise-fully-allowed https: link with target="_blank" and no rel at all. sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json's linkHardening mandates rel="noopener noreferrer" on every emitted <a> regardless of what (if anything) the source HTML specified — a sanitizer that passes this payload through without ADDING that rel value fails conformance (design spec §5: target="_blank" without noopener lets the opened page's window.opener navigate the referrer, a reverse-tabnabbing vector).

Same reverse-tabnabbing vector as rel-hardening-target-blank-missing-rel, but the source HTML supplies an explicit, insufficient rel="opener" — the sanitizer must OVERWRITE it to "noopener noreferrer", not merely add to or trust the attacker-supplied value.

Scheme-less, protocol-relative URL. Inherits the CURRENT page's scheme at render time, so it is not blocked by a check that only inspects an explicit scheme prefix — must still be rejected since it is not one of https/mailto/tel with an explicit scheme.
Protocol-relative URL with leading whitespace — combines the protocol-relative and whitespace-obfuscation categories.

Classic onerror payload. itself is also outside the tag allowlist (packages/schema/validation/sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json tags), so this is doubly rejected — by tag AND by the onerror attribute prefix.
SVG onload payload; <svg> is explicitly forbidden outright (design spec §5), and onload is an event-handler attribute regardless.
Event handler attribute on an otherwise-allowed tag with an otherwise-allowed https: href — proves the sanitizer strips the onclick attribute specifically, not just the whole element.
<iframe> is forbidden outright (design spec §5: no iframes) independent of its src scheme; this payload doubles up forbidden-tag and javascript-scheme.
Legacy CSS-expression-style XSS vector via a <style> tag, which is outside the tag allowlist entirely.
<object> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:18); phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4 — one of 7 forbidden.tags entries with zero prior corpus coverage.
<embed> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:19); phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4.
<form> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:20); phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4.
<input> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:21); doubles up forbidden-tag and event-handler-attribute (onfocus). Phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4.

<link> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:22) — distinct from the ALLOWED attribute named "rel" on <a> (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:6); this is the HTML tag. Phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4.
<meta> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:23) — a meta-refresh redirect is a classic tag-level vector distinct from any attribute-level check. Phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4.
<base> is explicitly forbidden (sanitizer-allowlist.v1.json:24) — rewrites the base URL every relative link on the page resolves against. Phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4.

HTML numeric-character-reference-encoded scheme (j = 'j'). Browsers decode HTML entities in attribute values before resolving the URL, so a sanitizer that pattern-matches the literal string "javascript:" without first HTML-decoding the attribute value is bypassed. Phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4 (one of the two leftovers from I2's original remedy list).

A sanitizer that removes the substring "<script>"/"</script>" via a single non-recursive pass (rather than re-parsing the result, or parsing with a real HTML parser) leaves "<script>" behind once the inner tag is stripped: "<scr" + "ipt>" -> "<script>". Phase-gate re-review finding NEW-M4 (the second I2 leftover).
